response.sql: WITH qualifying AS (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-'), per_patient AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_tat_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN qualifying q ON l.ID = q.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_of_pt_averages, AVG(avg_tat_diff) AS avg_of_tat_diff_averages FROM per_patient;

assumptions.assumption: A patient qualifies when a single laboratory record has both U-PRO exactly '-' and RA exactly '-', as the request's 'on which' wording indicates.
Once a patient qualifies, the PT and TAT-TAT2 averages use all of that patient's laboratory records, not only the qualifying ones.

Missing values are NULLs. AVG skips them, so TAT-TAT2 is averaged only over records where both TAT and TAT2 are present. A patient whose PT or TAT-TAT2 values are all missing has a NULL per-patient average and is left out of the outer average.
The text comparisons are exact and case-sensitive, so values such as ' -' or '- ' are not treated as '-'.
